sections.title: Faith and the Promise
observations: In this section, Paul emphasizes that the promise of salvation comes through faith, not through the law. He reminds the Galatians that they received the Holy Spirit by believing in the message of Christ, not by adhering to the law. This serves as a foundational truth for understanding the nature of salvation.

sections.title: The Role of the Law
observations: Paul explains that the law was given to guide and teach the people until Christ came. The law serves as a tutor, highlighting humanity's inability to achieve righteousness on their own. This section contrasts the temporary nature of the law with the eternal promise of faith.

sections.title: Unity in Christ
observations: In this part, Paul discusses the implications of being in Christ. He asserts that all believers, regardless of their background, are one in Christ Jesus. This unity transcends ethnic, social, and gender barriers, emphasizing the inclusivity of the gospel.

importantVerses.commentary: "So also Abraham 'believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness.'" This verse highlights the principle of justification by faith, which is central to Paul's argument.
"So in Christ Jesus you are all children of God through faith." This verse underscores the identity of believers as children of God, emphasizing the relational aspect of faith.

questions: What does it mean to be justified by faith rather than by works of the law?
How does the concept of being one in Christ challenge societal norms and divisions?
In what ways does the law serve as a tutor for believers today?
